name: Bull Call Diagonal Spread (Long Call Diagonal, Debit)
summary: Buy a longer-dated lower-strike call and sell a shorter-dated higher-strike call; a bullish debit spread whose short leg is sold repeatedly against a long-dated long.

legs.strike_rule: Lower strike, chosen by delta 0.60-0.75 (ITM). Deeper than 0.75 is the PMCC variant.
Higher strike, chosen by delta 0.25-0.35, and strictly above the long strike. Additional constraint: short strike >= long strike + net debit, so that both-ITM at expiry is still a profit.

max_profit: At the short strike at front expiry: approximately (value of the back-month long at that price and date) - net debit. If the short is rolled repeatedly, cumulative max profit grows with each credit collected.
max_loss: The net debit paid, realized if the underlying falls far enough that both calls approach zero. The debit-financing effect of rolled short calls reduces this over time.
breakevens: At front expiry, approximately long strike + net debit adjusted for the remaining time value of the long - solve numerically. Rule of thumb: spot must be above long strike + (debit x 0.6) at front expiry.

greeks.delta: net positive, typically +0.30 to +0.45 per unit (long 0.65 minus short 0.30)
greeks.gamma: slightly negative near the short strike, positive below it
greeks.theta: positive when spot is below the short strike; negative when spot is far above it
greeks.vega: positive - the back-month long has more vega than the front-month short

when_to_use: Bullish but not explosive view over 1-3 months, on an underlying in an uptrend (price > 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA). Prefer IV rank 20-50: low enough that the long leg is not overpriced, high enough that the short leg pays. The diagonal beats a plain vertical when you intend to sell the short leg more than once.
entry_rules: Trend filter: spot > 50-day SMA AND 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA.
Long leg by delta 0.60-0.75, 60-120 DTE. Short leg by delta 0.25-0.35, 21-45 DTE.
MANDATORY: short strike > long strike, and short strike >= long strike + net debit per share. This guarantees that if both legs finish ITM the trade is still profitable.
Short expiry must be strictly BEFORE the long expiry - never the reverse.
Net debit <= 2.5% of equity per unit.
LEVEL 3 OK: a short call at a HIGHER strike with an EARLIER expiry is fully covered by the long call. Submit as a 2-leg mleg; if legging, buy the long call FIRST.
management_rules: Close the short leg at 50-75% of the credit received and re-sell the next cycle (this is the income engine).
Close the whole structure at +50% of the net debit as total profit.
Stop at -50% of the net debit, or if spot closes below the long strike minus 1 ATR(14).
Trend stop: close if spot closes below the 50-day SMA for 2 consecutive sessions.

Roll the short up and out when spot exceeds the short strike and the short's |delta| > 0.60, but ONLY for a net credit and only to a strike still above the long strike + debit. If the roll cannot be done for a credit, close the entire diagonal.
Roll the long leg forward when its DTE < 45 or its delta drops below 0.50.
Max 3 units per underlying; total diagonal debit <= 15% of equity.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short call by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the short call immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05/share or |delta| >= 0.90.
Close the short call before the session preceding ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share - this is the most common early-assignment trigger for diagonals.
Close the long leg no later than 30 DTE (the theta cliff) or when its delta falls below 0.40.
Always buy back the short before selling the long.
Abandon rule: if the long call's mark is below 30% of the entry debit, close both legs.
assignment_risk: Only the short front-month call. Because the long strike is BELOW the short strike, assignment leaves the account short 100 shares fully covered by an in-the-money long call - the least dangerous assignment in the family, but it still creates an unwanted stock position and financing cost. Buy the shares back within one session and re-sell a new short call. Dividend ex-dates are the main early-assignment trigger.
buying_power: Net debit only. Because the short strike is above the long strike and the long expires later, Alpaca reserves the debit and no additional maintenance.
liquidity_needs: Long leg 60-120 DTE with OI >= 200 and spread <= $0.20; short leg OI >= 500, penny or nickel quotes. Underlying ADV >= 2M shares.
common_mistakes: Selling a short strike below long strike + debit, so that a both-ITM finish is a loss; selling the short too close to the money and capping the trade instantly; rolling the short for a debit and destroying the economics; letting the long leg decay inside 30 DTE; ignoring ex-dividend dates.
zero_dte_notes: The short leg should never be 0DTE on a share-settled underlying under this playbook; the minimum short DTE is 21 at entry and the position is closed or rolled by 14:30 ET on expiry day.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
